bib.title: Generative AI Design Patterns, Chapter 3. Adding Knowledge: Bass

question: How do you add knowledge a foundation model lacks (recent, private, or beyond its capacity) at runtime, and which patterns (Basic RAG, Semantic Indexing, Indexing at Scale) handle the problems that appear as the system grows?

results.claim: Anthropic's contextual retrieval reduced incorrect retrieval rates by 67% (reported, not the authors' experiment).

results.quote: Anthropic has demonstrated that contextual retrieval with this prompt structure and the Claude LLM has reduced incorrect retrieval rates by 67% consistently across different content domains.

results.claim: TF-IDF weight of 'Alexander' dwarfs that of 'Diogenes' on 200-character chunks of The Anabasis of Alexander, motivating BM25 term saturation.

results.claim: Basic RAG keyword retrieval is brittle to a synonym: asking about a 'broken' rather than 'ruptured' diaphragm returns a different, wrong action (replace valve-diaphragm assembly vs replace safety head).

results.quote: The previous answer asked us to replace the safety head, and the current answer tells us to replace the valve-diaphragm assembly. This is very bad.

limits: No experiments of the authors' own: the chapter is illustrative. Code examples are single queries on toy data (Project Gutenberg Anabasis, an equipment manual, a toy product catalogue, a 4-sentence similarity demo). No retrieval metric, recall or latency is measured.
The only measured-looking figure, a 67% cut in incorrect retrievals, is attributed to Anthropic without a citation in the chapter's reference list; the baseline and metric are not defined here.
Fig 3-11 'Degrading RAG performance with an increasing index size' is a schematic; no data given.

Claims such as 'domain-specific embedding models dramatically improve retrieval precision and latency' and 'strategic chunking often provides better retrieval performance than long context' are uncited.
MTEB ranks and context-window sizes are a June 2025 snapshot and have dated.

Internal numbering is inconsistent: Index-Aware Retrieval is 'Pattern 9' in the Pattern 7 example but 'Pattern 11 from Chapter 4' in Basic RAG limitations; Fig 3-1 text says 'Pattern 9 to Pattern 10'. Summary is deferred to the end of Chapter 4.
Table-embedding example normalises with StandardScaler although the text says scale to 0-1 (min-max).
practices: Ground the LLM by placing retrieved chunks in the prompt before the question; the model preferentially uses in-prompt information (priming). Pattern 6, Grounding.
Tell the model what to do when no chunk or order matches ('Say none of them'), and make the output schema allow it. Pattern 6, TIP.

Run an indexing pipeline in advance (batch or on new items) and a question-answering pipeline (retrieve then generate) per query; return the retrieved chunks with the answer for citations. Pattern 6, Pipelines.
Strip whitespace, attach source metadata to each document, split into sentence-complete chunks with overlap. Pattern 6, Indexing.
Do not ship Basic RAG as is; evaluate whether each added pattern brings quantifiable benefit before adding complexity. Pattern 6, Limitations.
Use an embedding retriever together with a keyword one (BM25); an embedding-only retriever struggles with product names and item codes. Pattern 6, Limitations.
If the corpus fits the context window, skip retrieval and use the whole document with server-side prompt caching. Pattern 6, RAG versus large context window.
Do not embed a whole book in a single vector; chunk into information-dense, self-consistent pieces. Pattern 7, Embeddings.
Choose a chunking method to fit the document: length with overlap, sentence, paragraph, document-structure, or semantic-shift. Pattern 7, Semantic chunking.
Convert images to text with an LLM description or embed them with a multimodal model; transcribe video and embed sampled keyframes. Pattern 7, Handling images and videos.
Chunk tables by whole table, sliding window with headers, row, or column, and keep table metadata in the chunk. Pattern 7, Handling tables.
Handle jargon with synonym expansion of queries and/or documents, keep directionality (ETF is an index fund, not conversely). Pattern 7, Industry jargon.
Prepend an LLM-written situating context to each chunk before embedding and BM25, caching the document in the prompt. Pattern 7, Contextual retrieval.
Use hierarchical chunking (RAPTOR) for long documents: cluster and summarise upward, walk the tree at query time. Pattern 7.
Save the scaler when normalising numeric columns, and design the embedding so numerics are not swamped by the text vector. Pattern 7, Example and Limitations.
Store document-, chunk-, domain- and access-control metadata; use it to filter outdated content, prune the store, rerank by recency and source, and detect contradictions. Pattern 8, Metadata.
Prefer pruning old content to retrieval filtering because a smaller index is faster. Pattern 8, Detecting outdated content.
Pick embedding models with long support life or open weights, since a deprecation forces a full reindex. Pattern 8, Managing model lifecycle.
Split indexes by domain and route, and index incrementally rather than fully. Pattern 8, Considerations.

terms.definition: make the LLM reply based on a set of trusted knowledge sources when generating its response
The tokens an LLM generates are much more likely to be related to the text that it encounters in the context.
preparatory step of building an efficient data store; retrieval is the runtime step of searching the datastore for relevant chunks
dividing text into meaningful segments based on their semantic content, rather than arbitrary length
addressing the loss of context in chunks that are too small by adding chunk-specific explanatory context to each piece of text before embedding or indexing it
an extension of semantic chunking that builds a reversed tree by chunking, embedding, clustering and summarising up to a single root; RAPTOR is the advanced form

terms.term: Retrieval filtering / document store pruning / result reranking
terms.definition: three uses of metadata for outdated content: restrict retrieval by date, remove old chunks, or boost recent or trustworthy chunks after retrieval
